subject: Urgent: Everleaf Health AZ2 cascade — containment & diversion plan
messages:
From: Sofia Turner <sofia.turner@everleafhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@everleafhealth.com>
Date: 2028-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production errors and latency spike in us-west-2 (AZ2)

Hi Logan,

We're seeing a sustained latency increase and a spike in 5xx errors from our traffic routed to us-west-2 AZ2 starting ~08:50 PT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to >7% and median latency tripled. This is affecting a handful of critical flows (patient intake, billing).

Attached a short timestamped screenshot and a CSV export of request counts. Can Redwood confirm whether this is an internal AZ issue or if something on our side triggered it? Our SREs are digging in but wanted to loop you in — this is P0 for our operations.

Thanks,
Sofia Turner
Head of Platform, Everleaf Health
sofia.turner@everleafhealth.com

Attachments: everleaf_prod-screencap.png, everleaf_timeline_20281108.csv

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Turner <sofia.turner@everleafhealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-08T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spike in us-west-2 (AZ2)

Hi Sofia — thanks for the heads-up and the artifacts. We're treating this as P0. Hannah (runtime on-call) and David (regional ops) are on this thread.

Immediate plan:
- Hannah: start a real-time diagnostic and share KV cache / connection metrics.
- David: confirm capacity and whether cross-region diversion is available and safe for Everleaf's pinned model version.
- We'll aim to provide a short containment recommendation in 30 min and propose a diversion if stabilization isn't seen.

Logan
Senior SDR, Redwood Inference

P.S. Marco/Sofia — if you see any change from your side please post updates here.

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Sofia Turner <sofia.turner@everleafhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-08T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spike in us-west-2 (AZ2)

Thanks — quick diagnostics below (summary):
- Observed: Backpressure on AZ2 GPU pool for the dedicated tenant slice running Everleaf's models. Queue depth rose ~5x starting 08:47 PT. KV cache hit rate dropped from 94% -> 68%.
- 5xx signatures: mix of model runtime OOM rejects (memory fragmentation) and occasional network socket resets to LBs. No indications of Everleaf client misbehavior.
- Attached: diag-snapshot-az2.txt with p95/p99 latency per shard, and a short timeline.

Containment suggestions (immediate):
1) Reduce incoming QPS to AZ2 by diverting non-critical routes to us-west-1 for 15–30 min (we can route by path hash).
2) Enable temporary token-level throttling for bulk ingestion endpoints (Marco — is that feasible?).
3) If diversion is approved, we should use the pre-warmed cross-region variant (model v2.3-quant) to avoid cold-starts.

Risk notes: cross-region diversion may add ~60–120ms median latency for some endpoints; it will reduce error rates and overall tail latency. We need authorization from regional ops leads for a diversion.

Hannah Schmitt
SRE — Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: diag-snapshot-az2.txt

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-08T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Action required: Authorization to divert Everleaf traffic from AZ2 -> us-west-1 (cross-region)

Team — escalating for exec authorization. Everleaf is in active production with a high-SLA contract; their error rate is material and should be addressed immediately. Summary:
- Impact: Everleaf experiencing >7% 5xx and elevated p95/p99 latency across multiple endpoints.
- Cause: AZ2 GPU pool backpressure + KV cache degradation; no customer-side trigger detected.
- Proposed action: Initiate cross-region diversion AB test for 50% traffic (non-rollback routes first) using pre-warmed v2.3-quant in us-west-1. Monitor for 15 minutes, then increase to 100% if stable.
- Requested approvals:
  * Vanessa: approve cross-region diversion for Everleaf (risk/financial sign-off)
  * Stephanie: approve exception for model variant fallback (we will serve quantized variant vs their pinned variant)

Attachments: cross-region-diversion-runbook.pdf, everleaf_timeline_20281108.csv

I recommend offering a goodwill credit for the impacted window if diversion is necessary — pending finance guidance. If approved, Hannah and I will coordinate a live bridge with Everleaf and AtlasCloud to execute the diversion.

David Kim
Head of Regional Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-09T15:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Action required: Authorization to divert Everleaf traffic from AZ2 -> us-west-1 (cross-region)

Approved.
- Financials: authorize up to a 4-hour diversion window and an immediate 10% one-time service credit for the incident footprint; finance/steward to formalize the exact credit.
- Ops: proceed with 50% diversion cut and validate model fidelity on the quant variant. If metrics (error rate, p95) improve to acceptable thresholds within 15 min, ramp to 100%.
- Communications: Logan — please coordinate an immediate customer update (Sofia & Marco). Stephanie — please be on standby for rollback/escalation.

Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---
Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai> to Everleaf (final):
Date: 2028-11-09T15:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spike in us-west-2 (AZ2) — diversion approved

Sofia / Marco — quick update: Redwood has approved a controlled cross-region diversion to us-west-1. We'll start with 50% of traffic immediately and monitor closely. Expect a customer-facing bridge invite in 5 minutes. We'll follow up with postmortem and any agreed credits once the incident stabilizes.

Logan Wright
Senior SDR, Redwood Inference
